To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Timor-Leste’s membership of the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN), and its relationship with the organization, is shaped by the way in which regional and state actors have adopted, and re-shaped, the externally-imposed definitions of ‘Southeast Asia’, ‘ASEAN’, ‘state’, and ‘region’.
Timor-Leste has been trying to ‘become’, ‘act’, and ‘see’ as an ASEANS state in order to gain membership.
Timor-Leste has been trying to shape its state and its region through the process of ‘becoming’, ‘acting’, and ‘seeing’ like an ASEAN member state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the regional and national levels of analysis are mutually constitutive, and how this is reflected in the relationship between Timor-Leste and Southeast Asia.
how the region and state have been shaped by the processes of regionalization and the implications of this process for the future development of Timor-Leste and the Southeast Asian region.
the processes by which the state of Timor-Leste, as well as the region of Southeast Asia, is being re-shaped by ASEAN and its member states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the region and state of Timor-Leste are being shaped by ASEAN and vice versa.
Timor-Leste has become an ASEAN state, but that it is not yet acting and seeing as one.
Timor-Leste and the ASEAN are both region-shapers and state-shapers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Timor-Leste has been successful in becoming an ASEAN member, but it is still struggling to become a Southeast Asian state.

Timor-Leste has been trying to ‘become’ an ASEAN member state through the development of its own statehood and the acquisition of the requisite institutional capabilities and behaviours, and ‘acting and seeing’ like an ASEAN member in order to generate positive consensus on its entry into the organization.
Timor-Leste’s membership in ASEAN is contingent upon its ability to demonstrate that it is a legitimate, acceptable and acceptable state in Southeast Asia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

regional organizations can be seen as ‘shapers of region and state’, and that the process of ‘becoming’ and ‘acting’ as an ASEANS state can be seen as an important aspect of Timor-Leste’s nation building process.
Timor-Leste’s membership of ASEAN is a process of becoming, rather than an outcome.
regionalism and statehood are mutually constitutive processes.
